title: The Parts Installer
briefing: Why build every tool yourself when thousands of programmers share theirs for free? There's a package called boardcheck that tests motherboards in one line. Install it with pip, use it, and write down exactly what you installed, so anyone can rebuild our setup.
hints: pip.install("boardcheck==2.1") installs a specific version. Only AFTER that can you import boardcheck. Try printing pip.list() to see what's installed.
boardcheck.scan(board) returns "PASS" or "FAIL". A dict comprehension builds results: {b["serial"]: boardcheck.scan(b) for b in boards}. pip.freeze() returns the requirements text.

pip.install("boardcheck==2.1") / import boardcheck / results = {b["serial"]: boardcheck.scan(b) for b in boards} / pip.install("rgbglow") / pip.uninstall("rgbglow") / with open("requirements.txt", "w") as f: f.write(pip.freeze())
bonus: Install rgbglow again and call rgbglow.glow("blue"). Then try installing a package that doesn't exist and read the error.
